questions.prompt: Paging divides a virtual address space into
options: Fixed-size pages that can sit in any free frames
One physical region that can never move
Files
Interrupts
questions.explanation: A virtual address splits into a page number and an offset. The page table turns the page number into a frame number.

options: The referenced page is not currently in a physical frame
The ALU overflowed
The cache is write-back
The process has exited
questions.explanation: The valid bit is clear, so the OS must bring the page in or signal the process. A fault is the mechanism, not automatically a bug.
traps: Treating every page fault as a program crash.

options: Recent page-table translations
Whole files
The ready queue
Assembly source
questions.explanation: A TLB hit avoids walking the page table. A TLB miss is not automatically a page fault: the translation may still be in memory.
traps: Equating a TLB miss with a page fault.

questions.prompt: Classic paging avoids external fragmentation because
options: Any free frame can hold any page
Every page has a different size that must fit a hole exactly
The disk is always contiguous
All processes share one frame
questions.explanation: Frames are equal, so a free frame is always the right shape. The last page of a process can still waste space inside the frame: that is internal fragmentation.

options: FIFO can cause more faults if you add a frame
OPT is easy to run without knowing the future
LRU always faults more than FIFO
The TLB replaces the page table
questions.explanation: For some reference strings, FIFO’s fault count rises when the frame count rises. LRU and OPT do not have this anomaly.

options: The page whose most recent use is the oldest
The page that will be used farthest in the future
A frame chosen with no rule
The page that was loaded most recently
questions.explanation: LRU looks backward. OPT looks forward and evicts the page used farthest in the future. LRU is the practical approximation.
traps: Describing OPT when the name was LRU.

questions.prompt: Optimal replacement is not the real online policy because
options: It needs the future reference string
It always faults more than FIFO
It requires pages of unequal size
It disables the TLB
questions.explanation: OPT is the measuring stick. A real system has not seen the future, so it uses LRU or an approximation.

questions.prompt: A page-table entry commonly needs room for
options: A frame number
A valid (present) bit
Permission bits such as read-only
The process’s source code
questions.explanation: The entry translates a page and says whether it is present and what the process may do. Source text does not live in the entry.

questions.answer: The machine spends most of its time paging because the working sets of the runnable processes do not fit.
questions.explanation: CPU utilization falls even while the disk is busy. The fix is to run fewer processes or give them more frames, not to schedule harder.
